newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George sees EMU "beauty and beast" scenario.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George sees EMU "beauty and beast" scenario.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Monday that European Economic and Monetary Union offered up the benefit of a fixed exchange rate but the potential hazard of internal tensions as economies struggle with one, central interest rate.

"The beauty is the fixed exchange rate but the potential tension is what I've called the beast," George told parliament's Treasury Select Committee. Noting a difference of three percentage points between UK base rates and the German discount rate, George said: "You can have quite a sharp divergence of cyclical positions (between different countries). That's the problem with a one size fits all interest rate."
He said it was quite conceivable that the one European interest rate could be too weak for Germany and too strong for Britain in the future.
"That's an example for the sort of tensions that could arise if you moved prematurely to monetary union."
